thread.title: Apple iPhone Unit Sales Seen Falling 5% To 10% In 2019 | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple iPhone Unit Sales Seen Falling 5% To 10% In 2019 | Investor's Business Daily
text:
A respected Apple ( AAPL ) analyst on Friday took an ax to his iPhone estimates for 2019. He now sees iPhone unit sales falling 5%-10% from 2018.
X TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said demand for Apple's iPhones is falling well short of earlier projections.
"2019 iPhone shipments (are) likely to be under 190 million units," he said in a report, according to CNBC . That compares with the current analyst consensus for 212 million units, according to FactSet.
He now expects iPhone unit shipments in a range of 188 million to 194 million in 2019. For 2018, Apple is likely to ship 205 million to 210 million iPhone units.

An increase in demand for less-expensive, older-model iPhones will not be enough to offset soft sales of the company's 12th-generation models, the iPhone XS and XR, he said.
Apple announced Nov. 1 that it will no longer provide unit sales figures for the iPhone and other hardware. Analysts took that as a sign that Apple expects its iPhone unit sales to turn negative soon.
Apple Stock Gets Two Price-Target Cuts D.A. Davidson analyst Tom Forte reiterated his buy rating on Apple, but cut his 12- to 18-month price target to 280 from 290. The new target reflects "a decrease in our near-term projections on concerns of lower-than-initially-expected iPhone unit sales," he said in a report to clients Friday.
Piper Jaffray analyst Michael Olson on Thursday cut his price target on Apple stock to 222 from 250. He maintained his overweight rating on the stock.
Apple fell 3.2% to close at 165.48 on the stock market today .
